questions.explanation: RAM stands for Random Access Memory — the computer's volatile working memory where data and programs in active use are stored temporarily. It is called 'random access' because any memory location can be accessed directly in roughly the same time. Contents are lost when power is off.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: ROM stands for Read-Only Memory — non-volatile memory whose contents are written at manufacture (or rarely) and primarily read, not modified. It stores firmware like the BIOS needed to boot the computer, and retains data without power.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: USB stands for Universal Serial Bus — a standard interface for connecting peripherals (keyboards, mice, pen drives, printers) to a computer. It supports plug-and-play and hot-swapping and supplies power as well as data. Versions include USB 2.0, 3.0, and USB-C.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: PDF stands for Portable Document Format — a file format developed by Adobe that preserves a document's layout, fonts, and formatting across devices and platforms. It is widely used for forms, e-books, and official documents because it looks the same everywhere.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network — a network connecting computers within a limited area like a home, office, or building. WAN (Wide Area Network) covers large geographical areas (the internet is the largest WAN), and MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) covers a city.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface — a visual way of interacting with a computer using icons, windows, menus, and a pointer, rather than typing text commands. Windows, macOS, and Android use GUIs. The alternative is a CLI (Command Line Interface), which is text-based.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation:
HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language — the standard markup language for creating the structure of web pages, using tags like

,

, and . It works alongside CSS (styling) and JavaScript (interactivity) to build modern websites.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What does 'OS' stand for in computing?
questions.explanation: OS stands for Operating System — the system software that manages hardware and software resources and provides services for programs. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS. It handles memory, processes, files, and input/output. (Open Source is a separate concept abbreviated differently in context.)
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What does the image-format abbreviation 'JPEG' stand for?
questions.explanation: JPEG stands for Joint Photographic Experts Group — the committee that created the widely-used lossy image compression standard. JPEG files (.jpg) are common for photographs because they compress well. Other image formats include PNG (lossless), GIF (animation), and BMP (uncompressed).
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: PNG stands for Portable Network Graphics — a lossless image compression format that supports transparency (alpha channel). Unlike JPEG, PNG does not lose quality on compression, making it ideal for logos, icons, and graphics with sharp edges or transparent backgrounds.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: PC stands for Personal Computer — a general-purpose computer designed for individual use. The term became popular with the IBM PC in 1981. It contrasts with mainframes and servers designed for many simultaneous users.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: WAN stands for Wide Area Network — a network spanning a large geographical area, connecting multiple LANs. The internet is the largest example of a WAN. By contrast, a LAN is local (one building) and a MAN spans a metropolitan area/city.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: BIOS stands for Basic Input/Output System — firmware stored in ROM that initialises and tests hardware during the boot process (POST) and loads the operating system. Modern systems use UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) as a more advanced replacement for the traditional BIOS.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: SSD stands for Solid State Drive — a storage device using flash memory with no moving parts, offering faster read/write speeds, lower power use, and greater durability than a traditional HDD (Hard Disk Drive). SSDs have become standard in modern laptops and high-performance systems.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: CD stands for Compact Disc. CD-ROM means Compact Disc Read-Only Memory — an optical disc that stores data which can be read but not written by the user. Related: CD-R (recordable once), CD-RW (rewritable), DVD (Digital Versatile Disc, higher capacity).
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What does 'ALU' stand for, a key component of the CPU?
questions.explanation: ALU stands for Arithmetic Logic Unit — the part of the CPU that performs all arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction) and logical operations (AND, OR, comparisons). Together with the Control Unit (CU), it forms the core of the processor.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol — a standard network protocol used to transfer files between a client and a server over a network. SFTP and FTPS are secure variants. FTP is commonly used to upload website files to a web server.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: SQL stands for Structured Query Language — the standard language used to manage and query relational databases (e.g., SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE). Database systems using SQL include MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and Microsoft SQL Server.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What does 'CPU' cache abbreviation 'L1, L2, L3' generally denote?

options.text: Levels of cache memory, with L1 being fastest and closest to the CPU core

questions.explanation: L1, L2, and L3 denote levels of CPU cache memory. L1 is the smallest, fastest, and closest to the CPU core; L2 is larger and slightly slower; L3 is the largest and slowest of the three but still much faster than main RAM. This tiered cache reduces the average time the CPU waits for data.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.explanation: DVD stands for Digital Versatile Disc (originally 'Digital Video Disc'). It is an optical disc format with much higher storage capacity than a CD (4.7 GB single-layer vs ~700 MB for a CD), used for movies, software, and data. Blu-ray discs offer even higher capacity.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What does the abbreviation 'OCR' stand for, a technology relevant to digitising documents?
questions.explanation: OCR stands for Optical Character Recognition — technology that converts images of typed, handwritten, or printed text (from scans or photos) into machine-readable, editable text. It is widely used to digitise documents, read number plates, and process forms.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What does 'VIRUS' stand for in the computing security context (commonly expanded as)?
questions.explanation: VIRUS is commonly expanded as 'Vital Information Resources Under Siege'. A computer virus is malicious software that replicates by attaching itself to programs/files and spreads, often causing harm. Antivirus software detects and removes such threats. (Note: this expansion is a popular mnemonic widely cited in exams.)
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What does the abbreviation 'IoT' stand for?
questions.explanation: IoT stands for Internet of Things — the network of physical devices (appliances, sensors, vehicles, wearables) embedded with electronics and connectivity that collect and exchange data over the internet. Examples include smart home devices, fitness bands, and connected industrial sensors.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: What does 'AI' stand for, and 'ML' as its common subfield?
questions.explanation: AI stands for Artificial Intelligence — the simulation of human intelligence by machines. ML (Machine Learning) is a key subfield of AI where systems learn patterns from data without being explicitly programmed. Deep Learning (DL) is a further subset of ML using neural networks.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following abbreviation expansions is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Option C is INCORRECT. RAM stands for 'Random Access Memory', not 'Readily Available Memory'. The others are correct: GPS = Global Positioning System, PDF = Portable Document Format, URL = Uniform Resource Locator. 'Random access' refers to the ability to access any memory location directly.
questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
